title: Quantization: canary rollout support for route-level toggle + mixed-traffic integration tests
author: Rafael Mendes
release_notes:
- Adds canary percentage rollout support for route-scoped quantization enablement (sticky sampling, guardrails, and audit-safe behavior).
- Adds integration tests to validate mixed traffic (baseline + quantized) and fallback behavior under incompatibility.
body:
Title: Quantization: canary rollout support for route-level toggle + mixed-traffic integration tests

Context
We already support route-level enable/disable for quantization (policy engine evaluates the route config and resolves profile in runtime). This PR adds canary rollout semantics so customers (and Redwood ops) can ramp quantization safely on a per-route basis (e.g., 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), while keeping sampling stable and auditable.

This is an implementation for ENG-18503, building on the route-policy enablement work from ENG-18451 and the Console/API surface introduced in prior PRs.

What changed
1) Canary percentage evaluation (policy engine)
- Introduces a deterministic, sticky sampling function to decide whether a request is eligible for quantized execution when a route has quantization enabled with a canary percentage.
- Sampling key is derived from stable identifiers where available:
  - primary: (org_id, route_id, customer_id) when customer_id is present
  - fallback: (org_id, route_id, api_key_id)
  - last resort: (org_id, route_id, request_id) (still deterministic per request, but not sticky across requests)
- Uses a fixed salt/versioned seed to prevent accidental reshuffles when code changes (see reviewer notes below). The seed is explicitly versioned in code (CANARY_SAMPLING_V1) to make future changes deliberate.
- Ensures sampling is applied after precedence resolution (org -> customer override -> route) so that overrides behave as expected.

2) Rollout safeguards / validation
- Validates canary percentage bounds [0, 100]. Values outside the range are rejected at config validation time (API write) and treated as 0% at read time as a defensive fallback.
- Adds a minimum granularity safeguard: supports 0.1% increments in config, but evaluation rounds to basis points internally (0..10000) to avoid float drift.
- Explicit behavior:
  - 0% => always baseline
  - 100% => always eligible (still subject to runtime compatibility checks and fallback-to-baseline)
  - in-between => sampled eligibility
- Adds explicit metrics tags to indicate canary eligibility decision (eligible=true/false) separate from actual execution mode (quantized/baseline). This helps distinguish “not selected” vs “selected but fell back due to incompatibility.”

3) Mixed-traffic integration tests
Adds end-to-end integration tests that run a single route under mixed traffic with canary enabled:
- test_quant_canary_10pct_mixed_traffic_distribution: sends N=10k synthetic requests with stable keys and asserts selection rate within tolerance (10% +/- 1.5%), and verifies stickiness (same key yields same decision across retries).
- test_quant_canary_respects_customer_override_precedence: org sets 50% canary, customer override sets 0%, route remains enabled; expects 0% for that customer.
- test_quant_canary_100pct_with_incompatibility_falls_back_cleanly: canary selects 100%, but runtime compatibility check fails (simulated “unsupported kernel on GPU class”); expects baseline execution with appropriate reason tag.
- test_quant_canary_0pct_never_calls_profile_resolver: ensures we do not fetch/resolve a quantization profile when canary is 0% (reduces load on registry + avoids confusing logs).

Implementation notes
- New module: policy/rollouts/canary_sampler.ts (and Go equivalent in gateway layer) to keep sampling logic centralized.
- Canary evaluation happens in the policy engine, producing a decision object:
  - quantization_enabled (bool)
  - canary_selected (bool)
  - desired_execution_mode (baseline|quantized)
  - decision_reason (e.g., CANARY_NOT_SELECTED, CANARY_SELECTED, OVERRIDE_DISABLED)
- Runtime uses desired_execution_mode as input but still performs its own compatibility checks (GPU arch, profile constraints). A later PR wires “auto-disable on regression” to act on these tags.

Files / areas touched (high level)
- services/policy-engine/*: canary sampling evaluation + decision struct
- services/gateway-config/*: config schema validation for canary percentage
- services/router/*: plumbs canary decision through request context
- runtime/telemetry/*: adds tags for canary eligibility vs execution
- tests/integration/quantization_canary_rollout_test.ts: new integration suite

Commits (squash merge summary)
- policy: add deterministic canary sampler with versioned seed
- config: validate canary_percentage bounds and basis-point normalization
- router: propagate canary decision and reason codes
- telemetry: add canary_selected + selection_reason tags
- tests: integration tests for mixed traffic + precedence + fallback

Screenshots / logs
- N/A (backend-only)

How to test
- unit: bazel test //services/policy-engine/... //services/gateway-config/...
- integration: bazel test //tests/integration:quantization_canary_rollout_test
- manual: set route.quantization.enabled=true and route.quantization.canary_percentage=10.0; send repeated requests with same customer_id and verify sticky behavior in request logs (canary_selected remains consistent)

Rollout plan
- Ship behind server-side feature flag QUANTIZATION_CANARY_ROLLOUT (default off).
- Enable for internal dogfood routes at 1% for 24h; monitor:
  - quantization_canary_selected_rate
  - baseline_fallback_rate (with fallback reasons)
  - p95 latency deltas segmented by execution mode
- Expand to beta customers only after validating stable sampling and low fallback.

Review conversation (highlights)
Benji Okafor (requested changes): The sampling key needs a stable seed; otherwise we risk reshuffling traffic if hashing implementation changes. Also please avoid float comparisons for percentage thresholds.
Rafael Mendes (author): Added CANARY_SAMPLING_V1 seed constant and converted to basis-point evaluation (int). Updated tests to assert stickiness across retries.

Jordan Lee (requested changes): Precedence clarification: do we apply canary before/after customer overrides? I want the override to fully disable quant for a customer even if the org route is in canary.
Rafael Mendes (author): Confirmed and implemented: precedence resolution happens first; canary sampling only runs if final resolved config is enabled. Added integration test to lock this in.

Sean Gallagher (comment): What’s the blast radius if the sampler throws or if config has a bad value? We should fail safe to baseline.
Rafael Mendes (author): Defensive behavior added: on any sampler error or invalid percentage, we treat as 0% (baseline) and emit a structured warning log + metric.

Mateo Alvarez (comment): For 0% canary, do we still fetch profiles? That could cause unnecessary registry load.
Rafael Mendes (author): No profile fetch when canary is 0% (asserted by integration test).

Logan Wright (comment): Please separate “selected” vs “executed quantized” for dashboards.
Rafael Mendes (author): Added canary_selected tag and selection_reason; execution_mode remains separate.

CI / checks
- buildkite/redwood-bazel: PASS
- unit-tests: PASS
- integration-tests: PASS (rerun once after flaky tolerance tightened)
- lint/format: PASS

Merge
- Merged via squash on 2025-01-24.

Notes / follow-ups
- Follow-up PR will wire canary selection + execution_mode tags into SRE dashboards/alerts and the auto-disable hook (ENG-18503 remaining work).
- If we need true user-sticky sampling for anonymous traffic, we may want to accept an explicit idempotency key / sampling key from the gateway in a future iteration (out of scope here).
